key: As Germ Celestial he is called Tanunapat, and Narasamsa born diffused in varied shape. Formed in his Mother he is Matarisvan; he hath, in his course, become the rapid flight of wind.
s: As the priests rub the fire-sticks and the flame is born, the hymn turns to the names Agni bears; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 3.29.11, reads them as stages: Tanunapat while an embryo in the sticks, Narasamsa once born, Matarisvan when he flashes in the mid-air.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 3.29.11, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 400415 (2024)

opened.locator: commentary on 3.29.11, and the hymn introduction

evidence.words: यदाग्निररणीषु गर्भरूपतया वर्तते तदा तनूनपान्नामको भवति । यदा जायते तदा नराशंसनामको भवति । यदान्तरिक्षे विद्योतते तदा मातरिश्वनामको भवतीति
evidence.gloss: When Agni exists as an embryo in the fire-sticks, then he is named Tanūnapāt; when he is born, then he is named Narāśaṃsa; when he flashes in the mid-air, then he is named Mātariśvan.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 3.29.11, at [262,11]). Sāyaṇa on 3.29.11 glosses each name by a state of the fire (garbha: an embryo in the araṇis; vijāyate: born and seen; mātari: the mid-air) and sums it in his own recapitulation, quoted in the evidence: in the fire-sticks Tanūnapāt, once born Narāśaṃsa, flashing in the mid-air Mātariśvan; Wilson’s translation of the verse follows the same scheme. ‘Stages’ is a fair word for his when/then series. Plain sense faithful: 3.29.1 to 6 and 12 are the rubbing of the fire-sticks and the birth of the flame, and 11 is the verse of the names; no four words of the key repeated. Names spelt as Griffith prints them. Revision 400415 dated 2024-02-02 by the Wikisource API. Evidence found in the packet. entry-check ok.
